MARKET.head: DBR Lafite merges China winery and sales under Leo Wang
MARKET.summ: Former Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang will oversee Domaine de Long Dai and the group’s China sales team as longtime winery chief Charles Treutenaere prepares to leave
takeaways: Domaines Barons de Rothschild Lafite appointed former Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang to lead its China winery and sales as managing director.
The move puts Domaine de Long Dai in Shandong and the national sales team under one executive for the first time.
Long Dai general manager Charles Treutenaere, nine years at the estate, leaves at year end and will assist the transition.

MARKET.head: Moët & Chandon tops Brand Finance wine ranking as Penfolds falls 32%
MARKET.summ: Veuve Clicquot recorded the fastest growth, while Australia’s Penfolds suffered the steepest decline, losing 32% of its brand value. China’s Changyu, a longstanding member of the top 10, fell 22%
takeaways: Brand Finance's 2026 Champagne & Wine 10 ranks brands by financial value via the Royalty Relief Method, not sales or market share.
Moët & Chandon ranked first at US$2.319 billion, up 12%; Veuve Clicquot rose 39% to US$1.429 billion, the fastest growth.
Penfolds fell 32% to US$776 million, the steepest drop, as TWE restricts supply of Bin 407 amid cost-cutting pressure in China and the US.

MARKET.head: WineGB to exhibit English and Welsh wines at Amsterdam trade show
MARKET.summ: English and Welsh wine has moved from a niche market to one of the most dynamic cool climate categories in Europe. Producers are gaining international attention for sparkling wines, as
takeaways: WineGB, the English and Welsh wine trade association, will exhibit at Wine Professional in Amsterdam in January 2027.
The stand is run with GREAT, the UK government's international communications programme, targeting Dutch buyers, importers and sommeliers.

MARKET.head: California Table Grape Commission hires Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie to lead Canada, Mexico and Central America marketing
MARKET.summ: The California Table Grape Commission has added Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as its Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico, and Central America
takeaways: She previously served as chief executive of the Center for Produce Safety and as international marketing director for American Pistachio Growers.
Her role covers working with in-market representatives, importers and retailers to increase demand for fresh California table grapes.

MARKET.head: ProWine Mumbai to showcase India's wine and spirits market to global producers
MARKET.summ: India’s growing appeal to international wine and spirits producers will take center stage at ProWine Mumbai this month, as rising disposable incomes, demand for premium drinks and new trade agreements open opportunities in the market
takeaways: ProWine Mumbai runs November 18-19 at Jio World Convention Centre, expecting 200+ exhibitors and 6,000 trade visitors.
Free trade agreements with Australia, the UK and New Zealand, plus EU talks concluded in January 2026, will cut tariffs on some imported wines and spirits.
Co-organized by Messe Düsseldorf India and All Things Nice, with 12 national pavilions and more than 1,000 drinks brands.

MARKET.head: Australian white wine exports to China more than double in volume in Q3
MARKET.summ: White wine export volumes to the market more than doubled, rising 143.6%, according to Wine Australia data. The growth comes as Australian producers seek a greater foothold among Chinese white wine drinkers, including consumers exploring alternatives to Burgundy
takeaways: Australian wine exports to mainland China rose 1.9% by value in Q3 2026 while global exports fell 7.3%.
White wine export volumes to mainland China rose 143.6%, with value up 51.9% to A$11.87 million, per Wine Australia data.
Red wine still made up 91.62% of Australian export value to China, while white wine held 7.14%.

CULTURE.head: Napa's 2011 reds, once panned, now drink well; growers say decisions matter more
CULTURE.summ: As unpredictable growing conditions blur the line between good and bad vintages, wine professionals are reconsidering how vintage quality is defined, evaluated, and communicated
takeaways: Napa's 2011 reds were rated poorly at release, with Wine Spectator giving 86 points and Wine Advocate 82.
Winemakers Steve Matthiasson and Ridge's David Gates say the 2011 wines now drink as well or better than at release.
Growers argue that winemaker decisions during the season matter more to vintage quality as climate change makes weather more erratic.

CULTURE.head: VinePair publishes its annual Top 50 wines of 2026 list
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Meiomi. Celebrate your holiday season to the fullest by bringing, or hosting with, the bottle that makes a lasting impression even after the last drop. From lush aromas of black cherry to warm notes of toasty mocha, Meiomi Pinot Noir is the perfect finish for all of your holiday moments.
takeaways: VinePair publishes an annual Top 50 wines list, with the 2026 edition discussed on its podcast.
Managing editor Hannah, who organized the Top 50 tasting, joined host Keith Beavers to discuss the selected wines.

CULTURE.head: Wine's cultural status is slipping as mocktails and coffee drinks gain ground
CULTURE.summ: I was re-reading an article titled “Is Free Trade Passé?” that the economist Paul Krugman wrote back in 1987 and it got me thinking about what’s happening in the world today. Here is my report. >>><<< Is Free Trade Passé?
takeaways: The writer argues wine has lost its once-broad status as a symbol of civilization and shared social drinking.
Evidence cited includes falling alcohol sales, fewer wine bottles on restaurant tables, and mocktail lists longer than wine lists.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story recounts how she came to work in wine
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers's VinePair podcast "Wine 101" features Alison Smith Story, of Smith Story Wine Cellars, discussing her path into the wine business.
The episode covers how people come to wine in the current era of the American wine industry, with family and community as the focus.
The episode is sponsored by Wines of Alsace, which promotes the French region's Riesling, Pinot Gris, Crémant d'Alsace and Pinot Noir.

SCIENCE.head: Burgundy estate uses electrical conductivity mapping to read vineyard soils
SCIENCE.summ: Electrical conductivity maps can reveal striking differences beneath seemingly uniform vineyards, but understanding what those differences mean is far more complicated
takeaways: Domaine du Cellier aux Moines in Givry, Burgundy, used electrical conductivity mapping of soils starting in 2021.
Mapping at 1.5 meters revealed limestone density differences, guiding over 30 soil pits, per agronomist owner Philippe Pascal.
In 2026, the tressed Pinot Noir parcel reached 13.6% potential alcohol versus 14.5% for the conventionally trimmed neighbour.

SCIENCE.head: AWRI urges users to update its agrochemical and MRL search app
SCIENCE.summ: 9 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated the version of the AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on both the Apple App … more
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute has released an updated version of its AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app.
The free app gives rapid access to information from the 'Agrochemicals registered for use in Australian viticulture' booklet.
Users on Apple App Store and Google Play Store are asked to perform an app update to keep receiving updates.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Eight impressive wines from leading independent wine merchant Yapp Brothers
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Yapp Brothers are based in Wiltshire, in the southwest of the UK, and are an important importer of
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Yapp Brothers, a Wiltshire-based importer and independent merchant, showed eight wines at the Bunch tasting, a collaborative event of independent UK retailers.
Domaine André Vatan Sancerre Les Charmes 2025 and Patrick Jasmin Côte-Rôtie La Giroflarie 2022 each scored 94/100 and 95/100 respectively.
Jasper Hill's Georgia's Paddock Shiraz 2023 from Heathcote, Australia, is organically farmed and retails at £52.

NEWSLETTERS.head: What the Hell Do They Mean?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Let’s play wine tasting note bingo, here’s TMC’s handy guide
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: It says 'minerality' is now used so loosely that it can safely be applied to almost any wine, and 'funk' is banned in Berlin and New York.
The author also lampoons inflated scores, such as 99.1-point notes and the use of '16.5' to signal an average wine.

NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Burgundy Region Quietly Absorbing This Year’s Rising Prices
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover how the Burgundy wine market quietly absorbs rising prices in 2026, revealing new trends and steady demand for fine wine collectors
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Comité des Vins de Bourgogne figures show Burgundy white wine sales rose 0.4 per cent in the year to July 2026, while red fell 4.9 per cent.
Mâconnais Chardonnay bulk prices fell, with Mâcon-Villages Blanc down 9 per cent and Bourgogne Blanc down 13 per cent, per the regional agriculture office.
Pouilly-Fuissé was valued at about €817 a hectolitre for the 2024 harvest, versus roughly €3,050 for Puligny-Montrachet.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Choosing Thanksgiving Wines
NEWSLETTERS.summ: No single wine pairs perfectly with the Thanksgiving meal, but many styles can shine on your table
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Chardonnay and off-dry Riesling are traditional pairings for the northeastern Thanksgiving meal, along with Pinot Noir and Gamay-based Beaujolais.
Sparkling wines, such as Champagne or Crémant, are recommended as low-alcohol, flexible choices that cleanse the palate throughout the meal.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Five Minutes with... Rick Rainey & Léana Godard of Forge Cellars
NEWSLETTERS.summ: On Cabernet Franc’s untapped potential, giving Finger Lakes terroir a seat at the table, and why it’s all about joy
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Forge Cellars, established in 2011 on Seneca Lake in New York's Finger Lakes, began Cabernet Franc with its 2019 vintage.
Forge now makes four single-vineyard Cabernet Francs from different soils, including Willow (sand), Railroad (gravel), Arlo (clay) and Bellows (sand and rock).
In 2023 Forge left stems out entirely to read each site's tannin potential, then reintroduced stems in some wines in 2024.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics should be just slightly more knowledgeable than their target audience, not vastly more expert.
Atkin says American critics are often expected to be superhuman tasters, while British critics are expected to be knowledgeable scholars.
Atkin criticises the typical 30-second tasting process, noting critics often assess tens or over a hundred wines in one sitting.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus alerts users to wines in its network from sources like merchant inventories, auction notices, and restaurant sales.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions and can upload images, and Orpheus connects them with the seller.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós of Penedès produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872, using Spanish grapes rather than Champagne varieties.
Cava gets its name from the cellars, or caves, dug to store the wine, and became a formal label term under Spanish law in 1972.
Sumarroca Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava 2022 from Penedès, made from Macabeu, Xarel•lo and Parellada, was aged 40 months and costs $28 Cdn.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing and was scheduled for Guangzhou on November 6.
Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but only a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
DCOOP's Airén and Tempranillo, and Ayuso and Campos Reales' Verdejo, were highlighted as easy-drinking wines at entry-level export prices.
